name: DLocal
thesis: DLocal is the 'one-API' cross-border payments rail connecting global enterprise merchants (big tech, streaming, marketplaces, SaaS, advertising) to the fragmented local payment methods of emerging markets across Latin America, Africa, and Asia -- pay-in, pay-out, settlement, and FX, in corridors where Adyen/Stripe-class processors have thin local coverage and licensing. The bet is that emerging-market digital-commerce volume compounds fast enough that gross-profit DOLLARS keep compounding ~25%+ even as the headline take rate (gross profit over TPV) structurally grinds down -- 1.05% (Q1'25) to 0.88% (Q4'25) to 0.84% (Q1'26) -- because that compression is the deliberate, healthy arithmetic of scaling volume with large sticky merchants and expanding into new lower-take corridors and payment methods, not pricing weakness. The proof points are record TPV (+73% YoY to $14.1B in Q1'26, well above the 50-60% guided range), 152% net revenue retention (existing merchants expanding hard), and gross profit still compounding +40% YoY to a record $119M. The structural risk is the mirror image: take-rate and gross-margin compression (39% to 35% gross margin) that eventually outruns volume so gross-profit dollars stall, plus EM FX / capital-control / regulatory shocks (Argentina, Nigeria, Egypt corridors), merchant concentration and the recurring governance-credibility overhang (the 2022 Muddy Waters episode). Management now steers to operating profit (Adjusted EBITDA was retired as a segment performance metric as of Jan-1-2026), guiding 50-60% TPV growth, 22.5-27.5% gross-profit growth, and 27.5-32.5% operating-profit growth for 2026 with leverage weighted to H2. Thesis intact while gross-profit dollars compound above the mid-teens, TPV growth holds the 30%+ floor, and NRR stays north of 100%; it breaks if gross-profit growth falls below ~15% for two quarters (compression finally outrunning volume), TPV YoY drops under 30%, NRR falls below 100%, take rate (GP/TPV) steps down under ~0.65%, or operating margin caves below ~10%.
key_driver: TPV growth x gross-profit-dollar growth x net revenue retention (volume must outrun take-rate compression)

tier_1_kpis.name: TPV YoY growth (USD)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <30% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs -- 2026 guidance floor is 50-60%; sub-30% means the EM-volume engine has stalled

tier_1_kpis.name: Gross profit YoY growth (USD)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <15% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs -- volume no longer outrunning take-rate compression (2026 guidance is 22.5-27.5% gross-profit growth). THE primary break: the whole bet is GP dollars compounding through the take-rate grind

tier_1_kpis.name: Gross profit over TPV (take rate)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <0.65% for 2 consecutive Qs -- an abrupt step-down beyond the normal scale-driven grind. The grind itself is expected and is NOT the break; an accelerated collapse is

tier_1_kpis.name: Net revenue retention (NRR)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <100% for 2 consecutive Qs -- existing merchants net-shrinking; the land-and-expand flywheel reverses (early-warning soft rule fires <120%)

tier_1_kpis.name: Revenue YoY Growth (USD)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <20% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (and <0% trips the universal contraction rule)

tier_1_kpis.name: Gross Margin (GAAP)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <30% for 2 consecutive Qs -- recent range is 34-39%; sub-30% signals mix/local-rails cost erosion outrunning the model

tier_1_kpis.name: Operating Margin (GAAP)
tier_1_kpis.current: ~17% (Q1'26 operating profit $57.2M ex one-off prior-years tax; reported lower)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <10% for 2 consecutive Qs -- 2026 guidance is 27.5-32.5% operating-profit growth; operating profit is now the company's primary performance metric (Adj-EBITDA retired Jan-1-2026)

tier_2_kpis.name: TPV by geography (LatAm vs Africa & Asia)

tier_3_kpis.name: Merchant concentration / top-merchant share of TPV

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Take-rate / gross-margin compression outruns TPV growth so gross-profit dollars stall (volume no longer wins the race)
TPV growth decelerates below the secular EM-digital-payments trend (engine slowing, not just take rate)
NRR falls below 100% -- merchants insourcing, multi-homing to Adyen/Stripe as they build local coverage, or churning
Loss or insourcing of a top-concentration merchant (revenue is concentrated in a handful of global accounts)
EM FX / capital-controls / regulatory shock in a key corridor (Argentina, Nigeria, Egypt, Brazil)
Renewed accounting / governance credibility event (Muddy Waters-style short thesis or restatement)
Competitive take-rate war as Adyen/Stripe/local PSPs deepen emerging-market coverage and licensing

break_rules.narrative: Net revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters -- outright top-line contraction. (FCF/OCF universals are deliberately omitted for DLO: as a payments processor it holds and settles merchant funds, so quarterly operating cash flow swings on settlement timing and is not a clean thesis signal -- the same treatment used for other float/working-capital-heavy names.)

break_rules_soft.name: nrr_below_120_2q
break_rules_soft.evidence_template: NRR {last_value}% below 120% for {periods}Q -- land-and-expand momentum cooling (hard break is <100%)

break_rules_soft.name: take_rate_step_down_2q
break_rules_soft.evidence_template: Gross profit over TPV {last_value}% below 0.80% for {periods}Q -- take-rate grind accelerating (hard break is <0.65%)

break_rules_soft.name: gross_margin_watch_2q
break_rules_soft.evidence_template: Gross margin {last_value}% below 33% for {periods}Q -- early warning before the <30% hard break

business_model_rules.narrative: Gross profit (USD) growing <15% YoY for 2Q -- the core thesis is that TPV volume growth outruns the structural take-rate grind so gross-profit DOLLARS keep compounding. 2026 guidance is 22.5-27.5% GP growth; sustained sub-15% means compression has finally outrun volume.
TPV YoY < 30% for 2Q -- the emerging-market cross-border volume engine has stalled. DLocal runs 50-73% and guides 50-60%; sub-30% breaks the secular-growth premise.

NRR < 100% for 2Q -- existing merchants are net-shrinking rather than expanding. At 152% the cushion is huge; a fall below 100% means the land-and-expand flywheel has reversed (merchants insourcing or multi-homing away).

Gross profit over TPV < 0.65% for 2Q -- an abrupt step-down beyond the normal scale-driven grind (0.84% in Q1'26, drifting ~3-5bps/Q). The grind is expected and healthy while GP dollars grow; a collapse to sub-0.65% signals pricing power lost, not mix.
Gross margin (gross profit / net revenue) < 30% for 2Q -- mix shifting to lower-margin large-merchant deals or local-rails / processing costs rising faster than net revenue. Recent range is 34-39%.

Operating margin < 10% for 2Q -- operating profit is now DLocal's primary performance metric (Adj-EBITDA retired Jan-1-2026). ~17% in Q1'26 ex one-off tax; sub-10% means OPEX growth (sales, compliance, headcount) has outrun gross-profit-dollar growth and the leverage story is broken.
